clue.text: French settlement — New Caledonia?

parts.note: nova is Latin for new
Scotia and Caledonia are both Latin names for Scotland

explanation.surface: A query whether some French colony in the Pacific might be called New Caledonia.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a Latin-to-Latin swap: New Caledonia (a real French territory) misleads, but the answer is New Scotland in Latin, which was itself first settled by the French as Acadia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canadian province began as Acadia, a colony founded by France in the early seventeenth century.

clue.text: Worthy, but incompetent

definitions.meaning: a worthy is a person of note, a dignitary
split as two words, incapable or lacking skill

explanation.surface: Someone is respectable yet hopeless at the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A worthy is an important person; split in two, the letters say lacking ability.

clue.text: See show and defend against critics

parts.note: V stands for vide, Latin for see, used in references
to indicate is to show or point out

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a performance and then stand up for it against the reviewers.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone of blame or justify them in the face of criticism is exactly this.

clue.text: Ignored ecstatic politician going round so-called Garden

parts.note: sent is old slang for transported with delight

indicators.note: the politician's letters surround the other piece, wrapping round it

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
Covent is the word that goes with Garden in the name of the London district

explanation.surface: A thrilled MP is snubbed while touring a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: COVENT GARDEN is a market district in central London. To be sent to Coventry is a British idiom for being ostracised, which the surface hides behind a garden tour.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means to be deliberately shunned, with nobody speaking to you.

clue.text: Well behaved worker in hospital

definitions.meaning: a hospital attendant who does non-medical tasks such as moving patients

explanation.surface: A hospital porter who causes no trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means neat and disciplined; the noun is an attendant doing routine hospital jobs.

clue.text: One stupid to lend, if not in good faith?

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters are muddled and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone would be foolish to lend money if the borrower is acting dishonestly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'in good faith' as honest dealing; in the answer it means the true religion, so an unbeliever is outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbeliever is someone outside a given religion, so not among the faithful.

clue.text: Those leading boys up rocky paths get the wind up

indicators.note: the letters at the front of each of the following words are the ones taken

explanation.surface: Lads climbing rough trails become scared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get the wind up' normally means become frightened; here it literally means bring wind up from the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Belching expels stomach gas upwards through the mouth.

clue.text: Free advertising's beginning to be eliminated from BBC

indicators.note: something is to be removed from the nickname that follows

parts.note: Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC

indicators.note: only the opening letter of advertising is meant

explanation.surface: Commercials are set to be banned from Britain's public broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC carries no advertising, which makes the surface plausible; its nickname AUNTIE loses A.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen a knot or bond is to release or liberate.

clue.text: Solid girl in the swim, coming to the top

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising from bottom to top means read upwards
the girl's name sits inside the word for a swim

parts.note: a dip is a quick swim
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl taking part in a swim rises to the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to the top' turns DIMARYP upwards; 'in the swim' looks like an idiom for being involved, but the girl goes into a DIP.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a solid is a three-dimensional figure, and this shape with a polygon base and triangular faces is one.

clue.text: Living further — the attraction of having skill with gun

parts.note: quick means living, as in the quick and the dead
on means forward or further, as in move on
a draw is something that attracts people

explanation.surface: A list of what makes life appealing ends unexpectedly in gunplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone fast at pulling a pistol from the holster, hence a skilled gunfighter.

clue.text: Part of joint to which musical group returns

indicators.note: returns says the word for the group is read backwards

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians

explanation.surface: A band comes back to a pub where it plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a venue; it is a woodworking joint.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry a mortise-and-tenon joint has a projecting tongue fitting into a slot.

clue.text: Military offender treated after duel

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier who broke rules receives medical care following a duel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a positional instruction but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In the forces this is someone who has committed a breach of discipline.

clue.text: Retired surgeon affected by skin problem

annotationWithheld.why: Retired surgeon affected by skin problem (9): the only parse is LISTER inside BED, where 'Retired' both gives BED and signals the containment (retired = in bed), one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Retired surgeon affected by skin problem

clue.text: Pick a light colour

definitions.meaning: the pick is the best of the bunch, the elite

explanation.surface: Someone chooses a pale shade.
explanation.definitionFit: The best part, as of milk's richest layer, and also a pale yellowish-white shade.

clue.text: Province of Orthodox Church a cypher represented

indicators.note: represented means presented again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coded symbol stands for a church region.
explanation.definitionFit: In Eastern Christianity a diocese or district under a bishop goes by this name.

clue.text: Writer turned into fat cat

indicators.note: the writer goes inside the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: turned says the writer's name is read backwards

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, American writer

explanation.surface: An author became a wealthy fat cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat cat' reads as one phrase meaning a rich person; it splits into wordplay and definition. 'turned' reverses the American writer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A big spotted wild species of the feline family found in Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Profligate accepted in a gang

indicators.note: the accepted word goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a band is a gang or group
done means socially accepted, as in the done thing

explanation.surface: A dissolute person is welcomed into a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Profligate and this word both describe someone unrestrained and dissolute.

clue.text: Herb runs into base after church

indicators.note: after places the next part behind the church abbreviation
the runs letter is put inside the word for base

parts.note: base means low or wicked
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A herb is planted in a garden bed behind a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a foundation noun but is the adjective meaning wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsley-like herb with aniseed flavour used in French cooking.

clue.text: Cover for vehicle parking, or another vehicle put outside

indicators.note: the second vehicle goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Options for sheltering a car: a covered space or another vehicle parked outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-sided shelter that keeps a car out of the rain.

clue.text: Sudden movement, followed by hesitation, makes greyhound cross

parts.note: a lurch is a sudden jerk
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A dog jerks forward, hesitates, and makes a racing dog angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry; it means a crossbreed. A lurcher is a British dog bred from a greyhound and another breed.
explanation.definitionFit: This British dog is a hybrid of a sighthound and a working breed such as a collie.

clue.text: Unfashionable US city was emptied of criminals

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: emptied removes the inside, leaving the first and last letters of was

explanation.surface: A dowdy American city was cleared of its crooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Fugitives from justice placed beyond the protection of law.

clue.text: Cop-outs amended in big organisation

indicators.note: amended means changed or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Evasions are corrected in a large company.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprawling organisation with many branches is likened to an eight-armed sea creature.

clue.text: One way or another, put facade round 'ouse

indicators.note: the word for putting on a facade goes around the other piece

parts.note: to put on a show is to put up a front
'ouse is house with H dropped, so home without its H gives the letters

explanation.surface: Somehow a front is put up around a Cockney's house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cockney dropped H in 'ouse tells you to drop the H from the word for a house as well; 'round' puts that inside the facade word.
explanation.definitionFit: By some means, in some unspecified manner.

clue.text: Shiny black metal from Italian city

indicators.note: the metal is taken away from the city's name

parts.note: Ravenna is a city in northern Italy
Na is the chemical symbol for sodium, a metal

explanation.surface: A glossy black metal comes from an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'metal from' as metal produced there; it means remove NA from RAVENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy black, like the plumage of the large crow.

clue.text: Rancour displayed by somebody in powerboat that's capsized

indicators.note: in a down entry, capsized means turned upside down, so read upwards
the person goes inside the vessel abbreviation

parts.note: MV stands for motor vessel
one means a person, somebody

explanation.surface: Bitterness shown by a person in a boat that overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice or bitter spite, figuratively poison.

clue.text: Port scoundrel out to lunch passed to left

parts.note: a rotter is a scoundrel

indicators.note: in an across entry, passing to the left means read right to left

parts.note: out to lunch is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A villain who was crazy passed the port to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is traditionally passed to the left at dinner, so the surface is a dining scene; MAD backwards gives DAM. Rotterdam is a Dutch port.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch city is one of the world's largest seaports.

clue.text: Old whisper circulating about new possession

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation for new
circulating means moving round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old rumour about something new is going around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' rearranges WHISPER to WERSHIP, and 'about' puts it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing as one's own, the state of holding property.

clue.text: Put out to graze many head of Hereford here?

definitions.text: Put out to graze many head of Hereford here?

parts.note: to run cattle is to keep them grazing, past tense ran
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many

indicators.note: only the first letter of Hereford is taken

explanation.surface: A place where lots of Hereford cattle are set out to feed.
explanation.walkthrough: Herefords are a breed of beef cattle, so 'head' means cattle as well as signalling the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A large farm for raising grazing cattle.

clue.text: Trained soldiers manoeuvre on the flanks

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers

indicators.note: flanks are the sides, so the first and last letters of manoeuvre are taken

explanation.surface: Soldiers who have been drilled carry out exercises on the wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Domesticated, broken in, no longer wild.

clue.text: Lonely wife takes drug with champagne

parts.note: grass is slang for cannabis
the Widow is a nickname for Veuve Clicquot champagne, veuve meaning widow

explanation.surface: A lonely wife consoles herself with cannabis and bubbly.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose husband is often away, leaving her alone.
